summary:
Red team of part 2 of the p-adic Hodge theory and p-adic geometry area: eight roadmaps and 68 stages (CrystallineCohomology 11, AInfCohomology 10, PadicHodgeTheory 10, PrismaticCohomology 9, PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology 8, CohomologyComparisons 7, DerivedDeRhamCohomology 7, FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory 6), with seven integrated decompositions. They were read against the sources, from TeX where available, and against parts 1 and 3 and the whole atlas. There are 46 findings: 7 high, 29 medium and 10 low.

The seven high findings:
(1) Scholze's finiteness and primitive comparison theorem (Sch13 Thm 5.1; BMS1 Thm 5.7) has no owner, although P8, CP.3, CP.4, AI.4–AI.6 and IG.3 rest on it.
(2) No layer builds the algebraic de Rham complex Ω^•_{B/A} or its divided-power version, although CR.2, CR.4, AI.4 and DD.2 use them; the fix makes DD.0 the owner.
(3) AI.2 cites a proof of Fargues' theorem that BMS1 does not contain (it refers to Scholze–Weinstein), and the proof's inputs, including Kedlaya's extension theorem, are unplanned.
(4) R07.4's Kisin functor, used by PR.7 and CP.5, rests on Fontaine's Kummer-tower equivalence and Kisin's lattice functor, which are unplanned.
(5) Tate's p-divisible-group theorems and Raynaud §4, which Faltings finiteness uses, have no owner.
(6) PR.4 attributes a smoothness hypothesis to BS22's étale comparison (Thm 9.1), which has none.
(7) DD.6 plans Bhatt's Theorem 7.22 as printed, and as printed it is false. Definition 7.20 asks only that b be a strict effective epimorphism, while the proof needs lci. The counterexample is F_p → F_p[x,y] → F_p[x,y]/(x²,xy,y²), using Bhatt's own Example 3.21. This is a source error for the errata register.

The medium findings fall into three groups:
- Missing inputs: arc_p descent for PR.4, the Tate–Sen theorem, slope filtrations for weak admissibility, Kedlaya's étale covers and the p-adic Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich formula, the dagger–rigid comparison, logarithmic Hodge–Witt sheaves, and log structures.
- Wrong or missing prerequisites: CR.4, AI.3, AI.5, AI.6, R06.3, CP.4–CP.6, PR.1, PR.5, PR.7, PR.8 and DD.5.
- Duplicates: B_dR^+ three times, Robba rings and dagger algebras, pro-étale period sheaves, the Koszul complex three times, Breuil–Kisin twists and syntomic complexes, the lci derived-PD comparison, and Kuga–Sato applications.

One library claim: Mathlib already has the tilt, Fontaine's θ, B_dR^+ and B_dR.

The low findings are locators, scope notes and presentation points. The coordinator extracted or reviewed 47 of the papers mentioning these roadmaps; their routes are not covered.

findings.claim: PR.4 attributes a smoothness hypothesis to the étale comparison of BS22 §9 and plans it only for 'the smooth formal scheme of BS22 §9'. BS22 Theorem 9.1 holds for an arbitrary p-adic formal scheme X over a perfectoid ring (derived prismatic cohomology, no smoothness), and its proof is carried out arc_p-locally on perfectoid rings, which are not smooth over the base. A smooth-only layer therefore misstates the source theorem and cannot follow the cited proof; the smooth statement is only the specialisation recorded in Theorem 1.8(4).

findings.claim: DD.6 plans to prove Bhatt's Theorem 7.22 for 'G-lci' maps exactly as Definition 7.20 prints it. As printed, the theorem is false. Definition 7.20 asks only that the second factor b be a strict effective epimorphism, not lci, while the proof sketch treats b with Theorem 3.27 and Corollary 3.40, which need lci (regular-sequence) quotients. Counterexample built from Bhatt's own statements, n = 1 and trivial log structures: F_p → F_p[x,y] → B = F_p[x,y]/(x²,xy,y²). The first map is smooth (log smooth of Cartier type), the second a strict surjection, and both rings are Z/p-flat, so the map is 'G-lci'. Yet dR_{B/F_p} is unbounded on the left (Example 3.21) while crystalline cohomology is coconnective, so comp_f is not an isomorphism.
findings.evidence: Stage DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6: 'Prove the specific G-lci/Cartier-type statement of Bhatt Definition 7.20 and Theorem 7.22, using the source's factorization condition and mod-p Cartier hypothesis; its Example 7.23 is a required failure test.' Source: Bhatt, p-adic derived de Rham cohomology, arXiv:1204.6560v1 (only version; TeX source https://arxiv.org/e-print/1204.6560v1, read 2026-09-24): Definition 7.20: 'A map f:(M → A) → (N → B) of prelog (0 → Z/p^n)-algebras is called a G-lci map if both A and B are Z/p^n-flat, and f can be factored as (M → A) →a (P → F) →b (N → B) with a an inductive limit of maps which are log smooth and of Cartier type modulo p, and b a strict effective epimorphism.' Theorem 7.22: 'Let f be a G-lci map … Then the map comp_f … is an isomorphism.' Its 'Sketch of proof': 'The map comp_b is an isomorphism by Theorem 3.27 (or simply Corollary 3.40)'. Theorem 3.27: 'Let f: R → B be a map of flat Z/p^n-algebras … Assume that f is lci.' Corollary 3.40: '… Assume that I is generated by a regular sequence.' Proposition 6.11: 'the natural map dR_{f_Alg} → dR_f is an isomorphism when M = N.' Example 3.21: 'we can take A = F_p[x,y]/(x²,xy,y²) … Then the derived Cartier isomorphism shows that dR_{A/F_p} ≃ ⊕_{i≥0} ∧^i L_{A/F_p}[−i]. In particular, the complex dR_{A/F_p} is unbounded on the left', preceded by 'this shows that derived de Rham cohomology cannot arise as the cohomology of a sheaf of rings on a topos.' The errata register research/errata/REGISTER.md records Bhatt 1204.6560 errata only for Remark 8.7 and Corollary 8.6.
findings.fix: Replace 'b a strict effective epimorphism' by 'b a strict map whose underlying ring map is surjective with kernel generated (Zariski-locally, or after passage to the inductive limit) by a regular sequence (lci)'. This is the hypothesis the proof sketch uses, and it holds in all three cases of Example 7.21. Add Example 3.21 with trivial log structures as a second failure test, and record the issue as a sourceIssue (kind: error, affects: a stated result, known: new — arXiv lists only v1).

findings.claim: CR.4 restricts the relative Langer-Zink de Rham-Witt theory to bases on which p is nilpotent, yet claims that this version supplies BMS1 §§10-12. BMS1 §§10-11 need Langer-Zink's complex W_r Omega_{B/A} over an arbitrary Z_(p)-algebra A, applied with A = O_C, where p is not nilpotent. They also need its continuous version (Def. 10.11), the Langer-Zink basis over A[T^{+-1}] (Thm 10.12) and base change along perfectoid maps (Prop. 10.14). AI.4 imports exactly these objects from CR.4, so under CR.4's stated scope BMS1 Thm 11.1 cannot be proved.
findings.evidence: Roadmap: CR.4: 'Construct the relative Langer–Zink theory for smooth algebras over a base on which p is nilpotent, with its relative crystalline comparison. This relative version, not just perfect-field de Rham–Witt, supplies BMS1 §§10–12.' AI.4: 'Construct the relative de Rham–Witt comparison using CR.4's Langer–Zink objects and the universal Witt-complex maps.' Source: BMS1 arXiv:1602.03148v3 p.81 §10.2: 'From now on, we assume that A is a Z(p)-algebra', followed by Def. 10.5 and Thm 10.7 ([51]), the initial F-V-procomplex for B/A. p.83 Def. 10.11: 'The continuous de Rham–Witt complex of a morphism A → R of Z(p)-algebras is given by WrΩi,cont R/A = lim_s WrΩi (R/p^s)/(A/p^s)'. p.84 Thm 10.12 ([51, Prop. 2.17]), stated for the Laurent polynomial algebra over an arbitrary Z(p)-algebra A. p.85 Prop. 10.14: 'Let A → A′ be a homomorphism of perfectoid rings'. p.86 Thm 11.1: 'Let R be a small formally smooth O-algebra. Then ... Hi(W̃rΩR) ≅ WrΩi,cont R/O {−i}', where O = O_C.
findings.fix: Extend CR.4 to cover: the relative Langer-Zink complex W_r Omega_{B/A} for every Z_(p)-algebra base A, as the initial F-V-procomplex; the basis theorem over A[T^{+-1}] and its integral part (BMS1 Thms 10.12-10.13); étale base change (Lemma 10.8, with Thm 10.4 of van der Kallen and Borger); the continuous complex of Def. 10.11 with Cor. 10.10; and base change along maps of perfectoid bases (Prop. 10.14). Keep p-nilpotence only as a hypothesis of the crystalline comparison (Langer-Zink Thm 3.5).

findings.claim: CR.5 builds the Kato-style theory of fine log structures: charts, exactification, the log PD envelope and the log crystalline site. AI.6 takes all its log inputs from CR.5, but CK §5, which AI.6 follows, works with quasi-coherent, non-coherent integral log structures in Beilinson's framework. Examples are the log structure on O_C/p with monoid quotient Q_{>=0} and its unique lift to A_cris/p^n; CK note that the needed log PD envelopes of non-exact immersions are not known to exist. No layer plans Beilinson's quasi-coherent log crystalline setting. The Binda-Kato-Vezzani route adds only the non-fine log-geometry prefix, not log PD thickenings or the crystalline site.
